tasks.instruction: Write a discussion response. An effective response contains at least 100 words.

professor.name: Doctor Diaz
professor.text: We've been discussing the idea that human well-being is not necessarily improved by ever-increasing production and consumption of goods and services. Some people argue that humans already consume too many goods, from clothing to electronics to food; they believe that excessive consumption has created serious problems for humanity and even the planet. Do you agree that excessive consumption--buying more than we truly need--has become a serious problem? Why or why not?

posts.name: Kelly
posts.text: I absolutely agree. We buy far more than we need, and that can't continue indefinitely. For years, people have used shopping as a form of recreation. The products bought on a whim are filling up landfills, and the energy expended producing the goods has created a global warming crisis. We should start gradually reducing consumption.

posts.name: Andrew
posts.text: I disagree with the idea that over-consumption is a dramatic problem. I agree there is some over-consumption, but it happens mostly with wealthy people. I think, in general, almost everyone else already buys only what they need. In fact, many people around the world are not even able to obtain everything they need.

tasks.sample:
I agree that overconsumption is a serious problem. 

First of all, purchasing too many unnecessary things is harmful to mental health. Consumers today, brainwashed by all kinds of advertisements, tend to buy things without careful consideration. When they finally face financial difficulties, they would reflect on those purchases and feel guilty. Even worse, it can be frustrating to organize and clean their houses if they have too many possessions, further hurting their mental health.

Besides, excessive consumption, as is usually considered a negative character, can reduce one’s reputation. In our society, overconsumption is often associated with extravagance and flashy personality, which can lead to social consequences. For example, couples may divorce because one buys too many products that the other deems unnecessary.

In conclusion, irrational consumption is indeed a problem.
